name: SMOL SmolDoc (document-level) — directed pairs
description: Google SMOL SmolDoc (document-level) MT evaluation across 100+ low-resource languages — the project's biggest breadth add. Each upstream file is one directed pair ({src}_{tgt}, mostly English-paired with a few Russian/Arabic/Chinese/etc. pivots). GATITOS is excluded (it is a lexicon, not an MT eval set). SMOL ships NO official eval split, so Champollion uses the FULL pinned release (at the commit revision below) as a deterministic, Champollion-defined held-out eval set; per-pair size + built-corpus sha256 are pinned from the revision (deterministic), so each runnable pair carries a verifiable integrity anchor. CC-BY-4.0. Domain 'mixed': general short factual content across many topics; domainDistribution is an approximate placeholder over general-informational domains, pending a per-corpus classifier pass on the built corpus.

download.instructions: Per-pair smoldoc/{src}_{tgt}.jsonl fetched from the pinned commit revision (immutable). SmolSent rows are src/trg sentence pairs; SmolDoc rows are parallel srcs/trgs document lists aligned element-wise. GATITOS excluded.

source.citation: Caswell et al. (2025). SMOL: Professionally translated parallel data for 115 under-represented languages.

license.notes: Published as training data; Champollion uses a deterministic, revision-pinned held-out slice as eval and sets doNotTrain to protect benchmark integrity.

usageRestrictions.communityNotes: SMOL ships as training data; the Champollion eval use is a deterministic held-out slice (the full pinned release). doNotTrain protects benchmark integrity.

contamination.reasoning: SMOL is a public training resource on HuggingFace, so frontier models may have seen it. It is professionally translated and covers very low-resource languages that are otherwise scarce, but its training-data provenance means contamination is moderate.
